necessary_context.content: E is a real finite-dimensional inner-product space with induced norm. For the selected unconstrained setting U=E, F:E→E satisfies <F(u)-F(v),u-v> >= ||F(u)-F(v)||²/L for all u,v∈E, with L>0. This implies monotonicity and L-Lipschitz continuity.
necessary_context.locator: Section 1.2, PDF p.4, Eq. (5); Section 2, PDF p.6
necessary_context.name: Space and cocoercivity

necessary_context.content: The paper assumes a solution of (MI) exists. With U=E this is a zero of F. The selected bound uses a zero u* minimizing ||u0-u*||.
necessary_context.locator: PDF p.1 (MI); p.5 standing existence assumption; p.6 unconstrained setting and Lemma 4
necessary_context.name: Existence and unconstrained inclusion

necessary_context.content: Set L_k=L, lambda_k=1/(k+1), A_k=k(k+1)/2 for k>=1 in (H) and Eq. (7). The paragraph following Lemma 5 explicitly states ||F(u_k)|| <= L||u0-u*||/k.
